title: Ella and John’s Wedding Registry
text:
Ducati Monster (for Ella)



Link embedded in image too


This is a practical mode of transportation fit for a fuel crisis. OK that’s only partially true. Lets start again. This is a reliable and safe mode of transportation… OK that’s definitely not true. What is true is decades of motorsport heritage and the most well known name in two wheeled transportation. I’m part Italian and it’s just about the only Italian word I know. Reliable? Practical? You’re asking the wrong questions! Is a Porsche reliable? A Patek Philippe practical? I don’t know - wrong questions.
But wait a minute, is the value proposition for a Ducati really as ostentatious as a Porsche’s or Patek Philippe’s? They all seem to carry a similar calibre of excess but the Ducati Monster cost less then the cheapest new car you can buy and gives you the performance of a supercar. The Ducati Monster gets better gas economy than a Toyota prius. The Ducati Monster oil changes cost $50. So yes, a Ducati is a inessential luxury item. But it still might be darn good value.
P.S. the answers to the questions you should be asking are

desmodromic valves,
0.3 hp/lb (0.5 kW/kg),
45,000 km service intervals,
supercar performance from a vehicle cheaper than a Suzuki Ignis (look it up).

title: General wedding details
text:
Kia ora all,
Our wedding will be held on the 23rd of January, 2027 NZDT. The ceremony will be at our house - 23 Kererū street, Taupō, New Zealand.
This site is to provide you with some details about logistics, and to help everyone stay organised. Specifically the yanks coming all this way - we want to help to make this a smooth trip for you, and appreciate that NZ is a long way to travel for a wedding. Hopefully after visiting you will understand why we have chosen to live here.
We hope this can be treated as forced vacation for all of you. The word “forced” meaning that you will feel strongly obligated to take some time off work, and treat yourself to a vacation in this beautiful country. We understand this is an expensive trip, and are not taking your attendance for granted.

title: General wedding details
text:
On the day information
For the wedding day schedule, see this page.

Venue
The ceremony will be held at our house - 23 Kererū street. It’s the mansion at the end of the street. Actually it’s not a mansion, but hopefully we will all fit. After the ceremony there will be a lot of mingling on our feet, so keep that in mind when picking shoes.


parking and travel
There is plenty of on-street parking on Kererū street. Taupō is also a small town with many cycle lanes, so drive, walk, bike - whatever you want. You will need to organise travel from the ceremony at our house to Acacia Bay Community Hall. Uber, taxis, and shuttles are available for this. See this page for contact details for taxis.


Dress Code
This is a lowkey event, but still a formal one. Dress in your best clothes, whatever that may be 😃. It’s a summer garden wedding, so leave the tuxedos at home and find some colours.


Wedding size
This is a small event with only our closest friends and family invited. Please no plus-ones or children unless specified. Exclusive, chic, fashionable 💅.

title: General wedding details
text:
Other Information

Accommodation Options
Taupō has many places to stay. We do not have any specific recommendations, but do recommend you use for following sites for your search:
Holiday homes
Airbnb
BookaBach
Because of the volume of accommodation options you can be choosy. We recommend getting something within a few km’s of our house.


Getting to NZ





There are a 3 or so airlines that fly to New Zealand direct from U.S.A. We have flown on a few of them, and from those experiences, recommend Air New Zealand. AirNZ has nice planes, service, food, and offer a great option those with babies of a thing called the “sky couch”. Air New Zealand is also a member of the Star Alliance so you can use points you have accumulated from other Star Alliance airlines (such as United airlines).
AirNZ flies direct to Auckland NZ from Los Angles, San Francisco, New York, Vancouver, and Houston. From Auckland you can fly to Taupō (a 50 min. flight). The flight from Auckland to Taupō is less than $80 USD so that probably makes the most sense. We encourage you to send us your flights before you book them, sometimes the slightly cheaper option will send you the wrong way around the world and be much worse.

title: General wedding details
text:
Things to do in Taupō
Please look at this website if you want ideas on things to do here.
Some of our recommendations/favourites are found below, here and here.
Taupō is a small town in the centre of the north island of NZ. We lived in Dunedin, Wellington, and have now landed here. Taupō is known for it’s natural beauty, big ass lake, tourist attractions, and proximity to the mountain. The natural beauty highlights include geothermal pools, the maunga Ruapehū, and swimming spots. Although there are many tourists, it still feels like a small town. Lake Taupō is the biggest lake in NZ, and feels a lot like lake Michigan in terms of its clarity and summer temperature.
Because of the tourist industry there is lots to do in Taupō. We have bungy jumping, sky diving, river jet boat rides, fly fishing, wine tasting, beaches.. the list is endless really. We’ve provided some recommendations below to at least give you a place to start.
